WITH RECURSIVE target AS (
  SELECT symbol_id FROM code.symbols
  WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/server/models.py' AND name = 'ApiModel' AND kind = 'class'
),
direct AS (
  SELECT cb.class_symbol_id
  FROM code.class_bases cb
  JOIN target t ON cb.base_symbol_id = t.symbol_id
),
anc(symbol_id, depth) AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id, 1 FROM direct
  UNION
  SELECT cb.class_symbol_id, a.depth + 1
  FROM code.class_bases cb
  JOIN anc a ON cb.base_symbol_id = a.symbol_id
  JOIN code.symbols s ON s.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
),
best AS (
  SELECT symbol_id, MIN(depth) AS depth FROM anc GROUP BY symbol_id
)
SELECT b.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, b.depth AS depth
FROM best b
WHERE b.symbol_id NOT IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM direct)
ORDER BY b.depth, b.symbol_id

request:
Which classes inherit from ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/models.py) only indirectly, i.e. through at least one intermediate class of this repository, and do not name ApiModel directly in their class statement? An import alias of ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/responses.py imports it as _Payload) counts as naming ApiModel directly, and a subscripted base such as ListResponse[T] counts as its class. For each, give the class symbol ID and the length of the shortest inheritance chain to ApiModel (2 when the parent class directly subclasses ApiModel).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
explanation: Finds ApiModel in models.py, computes the direct subclasses that name it (including aliased or subscripted bases via base_symbol_id), then recursively walks class_bases to get shortest inheritance depths. It returns classes reachable only through at least one intermediate class, excluding direct subclasses, with their minimum depth.
